question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual total of number_of_motorist_killed across NYC police-reported crashes.
options.denominator: None; count of motorists recorded killed.
options.reason: A direct annual fatality count is a clear description of the crash outcome, even though it is not exposure-adjusted risk.
options.answer: This crash dataset cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; its annual count of motorists killed in NYC police-reported crashes was 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: The requested per-mile question is only partly answerable: this line charts the annual sum of motorists recorded killed in all NYC police-reported crashes, grouped by crash-date calendar year for 2013–2025. The count was 110 in 2013 and 81 in 2025, a defensible direct tally of the recorded fatal outcome but without an exposure denominator. Per-mile risk remains unanswered because the data has no miles-driven measure and this count does not adjust for travel exposure. options.metric: For each calendar year, 100 times the number of police-reported crash rows with number_of_motorist_killed at least 1 divided by all police-reported crash rows.
options.denominator: All NYC police-reported crashes in the year; the data check found no missing motorist-death counts, so no denominator rows are removed.
options.reason: The fraction of crashes with any motorist death captures fatal-crash incidence while counting each crash once regardless of how many motorists were killed.
options.answer: This crash dataset cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; crashes with at least one motorist death were 0.0501% of reported crashes in 2013 and 0.0877% in 2025.
options.interpretation: The requested per-mile question is only partly answerable: this line charts 100 times crashes with at least one motorist killed divided by all NYC police-reported crashes, grouped by crash-date calendar year for 2013–2025. The share was 0.0501% in 2013 and 0.0877% in 2025; this crash-level fraction is defensible for fatal-crash incidence and counts each crash once, even if multiple motorists died. It leaves per-mile risk unanswered because the data has no miles-driven denominator, and this is not an individual motorist's probability of death. options.metric: For each calendar year, 1,000 times the sum of number_of_motorist_killed divided by the number of police-reported NYC crash rows.
options.denominator: All NYC police-reported crashes in the year; the data check found no missing motorist-death counts, so no denominator rows are removed; scale the rate to 1,000 crashes.
options.reason: Deaths per 1,000 reported crashes normalizes the death count to the crash volume and retains multiple deaths in a single crash.
options.answer: This crash dataset cannot establish whether per-mile risk declined; motorists killed per 1,000 reported crashes were 0.540 in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025.
